validated_results.title: The role of MTNR1B polymorphism on circadian rhythm-related cancer: A UK Biobank cohort study.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: Effects of green tea on prostate carcinogenesis in rat models and a human prostate cancer xenograft model.
validated_results.reason: Caffeine exposure was tested only in rat carcinogenesis models and human tumor xenografts in nude mice, so this is exclusively preclinical evidence.

validated_results.title: Effects of green tea on prostate carcinogenesis in rat models and a human prostate cancer xenograft model.
validated_results.reason: Green tea infusion and extract were administered in drinking water to rats and nude mice bearing xenografts, making the study exclusively animal/preclinical.

validated_results.title: Effects of green tea on prostate carcinogenesis in rat models and a human prostate cancer xenograft model.
validated_results.reason: Tea exposure was evaluated only in rat prostate carcinogenesis and mouse xenograft/allograft models without human participants.

validated_results.title: Dairy consumption and risks of total and site-specific cancers in Chinese adults: an 11-year prospective study of 0.5 million people.
validated_results.reason: The abstract reports dairy associations for total, liver, breast, lymphoma and colorectal cancers only, with no separable prostate cancer incidence result.

validated_results.title: Regular, Long-Duration Multivitamin Use and Risk of Overall and Aggressive Prostate Cancer in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 48,137 men reporting multivitamin supplement use and incident overall and aggressive prostate cancer with hazard ratios and confidence intervals.

extraction.comparison_type: Men using multivitamins 10 or more tablets per week versus never-users (advanced prostate cancer)
extraction.population: Male health professionals in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 48,137 men from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study were followed from 1986 to 2017.

cases.excerpt: We documented 7,108 incident prostate cancer cases including 564 advanced and 1,065 lethal.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who used multivitamin 10 or more tablets per week had similar risk of advanced (HR: 1.14, 95% CI: 0.77-1.70, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 0.80-1.44, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.59) prostate cancer, and multivitamin use of 15 years or more was not associated with risk of advanced (HR: 1.10, 95% CI: 0.80-1.50, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.83-1.31, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.13) prostate cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who used multivitamin 10 or more tablets per week had similar risk of advanced (HR: 1.14, 95% CI: 0.77-1.70, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 0.80-1.44, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.59) prostate cancer, and multivitamin use of 15 years or more was not associated with risk of advanced (HR: 1.10, 95% CI: 0.80-1.50, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.83-1.31, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.13) prostate cancer.

comparison.excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who used multivitamin 10 or more tablets per week

design.excerpt: Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate multivariable hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of multivitamin use and incidence of prostate cancer.

timing.excerpt: Multivitamin use and frequency were self-reported at baseline and updated biennially.

continent.excerpt: Multivitamin supplement is commonly used among older adults in the United States.

location.excerpt: among older adults in the United States

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Multivitamin use and frequency were self-reported at baseline and updated biennially.

validated_results.title: Adherence to a cholesterol-lowering diet and the risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Legume intake is only one of seven indicators within a composite cholesterol-lowering diet score and no legume-specific prostate cancer estimate is reported.

validated_results.title: Adherence to a cholesterol-lowering diet and the risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Monounsaturated fatty acid intake is embedded in the composite adherence score, with only the overall score association reported and no MUFA-specific estimate.

validated_results.title: Adherence to a cholesterol-lowering diet and the risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Seeds/corn oil intake contributes to the multi-component cholesterol-lowering diet index without any separable oil-specific prostate cancer risk estimate.

validated_results.title: Association between circulating vitamin E and ten common cancers: evidence from large-scale Mendelian randomization analysis and a longitudinal cohort study.
validated_results.reason: The report uses Mendelian randomization or genetic instruments, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: The Impact of Lifestyle on Prostate Cancer: A Road to the Discovery of New Biomarkers.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of lifestyle and candidate biomarkers for prostate cancer, mentioning vitamin D-binding protein only incidentally without original data.

validated_results.title: Chemotherapeutic Activities of Dietary Phytoestrogens against Prostate Cancer: From Observational to Clinical Studies.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of dietary phytoestrogens and prostate cancer rather than an original human study of Western dietary pattern and incidence.
